items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: What they do in the day was nothing, isn't anything new to Duke Ellington's original orchestra. He had men like Bubba Miley in the small band, and he had men like Tricky Sand. He had men like Bigger in the small band.

ctx.x: Did Ellington write much of that out at all? So when we say like black and tan fantasy, when you make that up?

Well, it comes from improvising. Black and tan fantasy had a score to it, but he had thought that the organization had so many great men in it, they could improvise. And they could put in things that would make Mr. Ellington smile and everybody else, because it was out the ordinary. And the first big band had individuals to get up and play something. What they do in the day was nothing, isn't anything new to Duke Ellington's original orchestra. He had men like Bubba Miley in the small band, and he had men like…
One time Barney told me something about how you all took the tune, that was one of Oliver's numbers, I think, in the Camp Meeting Blues. And you were part of that bar, the Creole Love.

items.title: Wellman Braud Interview, 1958-03-31
items.q: But Elgin arranges his own music, but then at the same time, he could get a lot of ideas, too, after he would hear a record.

ctx.x: One time Barney told me something about how you all took the tune, that was one of Oliver's numbers, I think, in the Camp Meeting Blues. And you were part of that bar, the Creole Love.

Yeah, Creole Love called, and we also, high number we had written by Lorenzo Teal, Mood Enigo. Oh, was that really? Oh, yeah, that was really. But you see, the Ellington is a doctor of music, I'll call him, because he can make a tune a little better and sound a little better than what it is. It'll come from his brain, it still comes from the same thing of improvising. Now, I see in places, I take an eighth note, if it's on the score, and I can make a thirty-second note out of it, but I know where to put it at.…
In the old days, before you, when you were just a kid and heard the first bass players, how many beats in a major did they play? Did they play something like that? Two beats.
